rationale: The workflow is a single-job schedule/workflow_dispatch CompatHelper job that installs Julia and the CompatHelper package, then runs a compatibility check. Historical runs are short (about 2-3 minutes) and consistently successful, with no evidence of runaway or overlapping runs. Evaluated patterns: P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (dependency caching) is not supported because the required cache-input precondition (a verifiable lockfile/environment file such as Manifest.toml) cannot be confirmed from the repository files, and an incorrect cache key could serve stale packages to a compatibility-checking tool; P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT/P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT have no runaway-run evidence in the history (all runs complete quickly), so a timeout would not save observed time; P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE is contraindicated because CompatHelper depends on the external General registry, not only repository changes; P-LIT-FAIL-FAST/P-LIT-SELECT/P-LIT-BAZEL-* do not apply (no matrix, no tests, no Bazel); P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE/P-LIT-SKIP-WORKFLOW lack an approved pause/skip policy. No supported optimization has all preconditions verifiably met while preserving intended coverage, so no change is made.
